title: GONE in 360 seconds: gentleMACS Octo Dissociator-based Nuclei Extraction
author: Deepak Balamurali

steps.title: Pre‑cool equipment and prepare buffers
steps.instruction: Cool all buffers and consumables that will contact the sample (gentleMACS C Tubes, SmartStrainers) at 4 °C overnight; place gentleMACS Octo Coolers at –20 °C overnight; pre‑cool the centrifuge to 4 °C; add RNase inhibitor to pre‑cooled 4 mL Nuclei Extraction Buffer to a final concentration of 0.2 U/µL per extraction; prepare nuclei separation buffer by diluting MACS BSA stock 1:250 (0.04 % final) and Nuclei Extraction Buffer 1:7 (14 % final) in PBS pH 7.2, adding RNase inhibitor (0.2 U/µL) if RNA downstream applications are planned.

steps.title: Prepare tissue pieces
steps.instruction: Retrieve 50–100 mg fresh or frozen tissue, cut into small pieces with sterile forceps and a surgical blade before freezing, keeping the tissue from fully thawing.

steps.title: Load tissue and run dissociation
steps.instruction: Transfer the cut tissue pieces to a pre‑cooled gentleMACS C Tube containing 2 mL ice‑cold lysis (Nuclei Extraction) buffer, ensuring the tissue floats freely; close the tube, place it on the gentleMACS Dissociator, add pre‑cooled Octo Coolers onto the tubes, run program 4C_nuclei_1 on the gentleMACS Octo Dissociator, then immediately detach the C Tube and place it on ice.

steps.title: Filter nuclei (70 µm) and pellet
steps.instruction: Apply the nuclei suspension to a 70 µm MACS SmartStrainer in a 15 mL tube and wash the strainer with 2 mL ice‑cold Nuclei Extraction Buffer; discard the strainer, centrifuge the filtrate at 300 × g, 4 °C for 5 min, aspirate the supernatant completely, and resuspend the pellet in ice‑cold nuclei separation buffer by pipetting up and down 10 times.

steps.title: Filter nuclei (30 µm) for purification
steps.instruction: Apply the resuspended nuclei to a 30 µm MACS SmartStrainer in a 15 mL tube; collect the flowthrough (nuclei suspension) for immediate downstream purification.

steps.title: Count and concentrate nuclei
steps.instruction: Determine the nucleus number using an automated cell counter or Neubauer chamber; centrifuge the suspension at 300 × g, 4 °C for 5 min, remove the supernatant completely, and resuspend 1 × 10⁶ nuclei in 450 µL nuclei separation buffer.

steps.title: Magnetic labeling and purification
steps.instruction: Add 50 µL Anti‑Nucleus MicroBeads to the 450 µL nuclei suspension, mix well and incubate 15 min at 2–8 °C; add 2 mL nuclei separation buffer and transfer the mixture onto a MACS column placed in the magnetic field of a QuadroMACS or MidiMACS separator; rinse the column with 3 mL nuclei separation buffer, apply the nuclei suspension and collect the flowthrough (debris); wash the column twice with 1 mL nuclei separation buffer, combining all wash‑throughs with the previous flowthrough; remove the column, place it on a collection tube, add the appropriate volume of nuclei separation buffer, and immediately flush out the magnetically labeled nuclei by firmly pushing the plunger. Collect the purified nuclei for downstream applications such as single‑nuclei RNA‑seq.

steps.title: Optional quality control
steps.instruction: Add DAPI staining solution to a small aliquot of the nuclei suspension to a final concentration of 0.25 µg/mL, mix gently by inversion, incubate 5 min at 4 °C, then load the sample on a hemocytometer or flow cytometer and analyze according to the instrument’s recommendations.
